chunks: 5067 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abbad ibn Suhayb, who said:
Abu Abdullah عليه السلام was asked about a Christian who slanderously accused a Muslim and said to him, “O adulterer.”

He عليه السلام said: “He is to be flogged eighty lashes for the right of the Muslim, and eighty lashes minus one for the sanctity of Islam. His head is to be shaved, and he is to be paraded among the people of his religion so that others may be deterred.”

key_terms.قَذَفَ: falsely accused with a slanderous allegation of zina
key_terms.لِحَقِّ الْمُسْلِمِ: for the violated right due to the Muslim
key_terms.لِحُرْمَةِ الْإِسْلَامِ: for violating the sanctity of Islam
key_terms.لِكَيْ يُنَكَّلَ غَيْرُهُ: so that others may be deterred by the punishment
key_terms.مُسْلِمًا: the Muslim whose honor and right were violated
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيٍّ: a Christian subject mentioned in the legal case
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to be flogged as a legal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment in Shia hadith for a Christian who falsely accuses a Muslim of zina?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a Christian who falsely accuses a Muslim of zina. It sets out a compounded punishment tied both to the violated right of the Muslim and to the sanctity of Islam, along with a public disciplinary measure intended to deter others.
